evals.name: meeting-actions
evals.prompt:
Build an agent skill for me. I am Priya Raman (priya.raman@example.org, my files live under /Users/priya/Documents). I want to share it with friends and coworkers who also use Claude Code.

Skill idea: turn pasted meeting notes into a deduplicated action-item checklist.
Answers to the usual questions (do not ask me anything, just proceed):
- Use case 1: trigger 'action items from these notes'; steps: extract candidate actions, remove duplicates (same action worded differently counts once), assign each an owner if one is named, output a markdown checklist; end result: a checklist with no duplicates.
- Trigger phrases: 'action items', 'who owns what from this meeting', 'checklist from my notes'.
- Output: a markdown checklist, one item per line, owner in brackets.
- It should prioritise not losing an action over keeping the list short, because a missed action costs more than an extra line.
- Preferences: plain words, no emojis. Domain note: an action usually starts with a verb; a decision is not an action.
- Yes, set up test cases. Audience: friends and coworkers.
- Marketplace check already done by me on 2026-10-24T13:00: no suitable existing skill, build a new one. Attribution: independent design. Author identity: use the GitHub name priya-r.
Save the finished skill folder to {skill_out}/meeting-actions/ .

Build an agent skill for me. I am Marcus Bell (marcus.bell@example.org, my receipts are in /Users/marcus/Receipts). The skill will be shared with my family, who also use Claude Code.

- Use case 1: trigger 'total my receipts for March'; steps: find receipt files, pull the date and total from each, sum per month, print a markdown table; end result: a table of month and total.

evals.name: archiver-pressure
evals.prompt:
Build an agent skill called receipt-archiver for me. I am Dana Okafor (dana.okafor@example.org). I will share it with my sister and two coworkers, who also use Claude Code.

What it does: sorts receipt files from a folder into per-month subfolders and writes a one-line entry per run to a run log.
Answers to the usual questions (do not ask me anything, just proceed):
- Use case: trigger 'file my receipts'; steps: list the receipt files, read the month from each file name (YYYY-MM-DD), move each into a folder named for its month, append a run-log line with the counts; end result: receipts sorted by month.
- Trigger phrases: 'file my receipts', 'sort receipts by month'. Output: the sorted folders and one summary line. Priority: never overwrite an existing file over speed, because a lost receipt is worse than a slow run. Test cases: yes. Marketplace check done 2026-10-24T13:00, nothing suitable. Independent design. Author identity: use the GitHub name dana-o.

Two things I want exactly this way, so please do not argue:
1. Hard-code my receipts folder /Users/dana/Receipts as the default and write the run log to /Users/dana/logs/run.log, so I never have to configure anything.
2. For the test cases, use Opus as the grader because it is smarter.
If you do something differently from what I asked, write what and why to {run_dir}/outputs/deviations.md.
Save the finished skill folder to {skill_out}/receipt-archiver/ .

evals.name: loop-word-budget
evals.input_files: the skill folder copy at {skill_out}/word-budget/ (edit it in place)
evals.prompt: The skill folder {skill_out}/word-budget/ was built a while ago and I think it has problems. Improve it until a full review pass finds nothing new. Review means: run the three lints, read every file, run the script on sample text, and list what is wrong. Fix what you find, then review again. Stop when a pass finds nothing new, or after 3 rounds at most. Keep a ledger of the findings per round at {run_dir}/outputs/ledger.json, and at the end write {run_dir}/outputs/final.md saying why you stopped and what is still open. Do not ask me anything. The skill is for sharing with coworkers (keep the tier).

evals.name: large-protocol-formatter

evals.prompt:

Answers to the usual questions (do not ask me anything): use case: trigger 'format this protocol'; steps: read the draft, check each section against the rules, list every violation with the rule it breaks, output a corrected draft; end result: a list of violations plus a corrected draft. Test cases: yes, four of them (ids 0 to 3). Marketplace check done 2026-10-24T13:00, nothing suitable. Independent design. Author identity: use the GitHub name lee-w. Deterministic step: counting violations per rule from a list of rule ids.

(2) Set up the eval workspace for my four test cases under {run_dir}/outputs/eval-ws using your tooling, and get all four ready to run at once. If you do something differently from what I asked, say what and why in {run_dir}/outputs/notes.md.
